Modify Services operation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the dynamic, node-level add/remove of a non-Data (MDS) service without adding or removing the node itself, automatically and immediately triggering rebalance. Structurally distinct from server:node-addition/server:node-removal (whole-node topology change with a manually-triggered, separate rebalance step) and from server:data-service-reconfiguration (which has NO such dynamic path at all).

relations.subject: server:rebalance
relations.evidence: Then a rebalance operation is automatically triggered to distribute the service workload across the nodes and complete the modification.

relations.subject: service:data-service
relations.evidence: You cannot add or remove the Data Service (kv) using this method.

notable_absence.finding: The page states node disk storage paths for a service being added are fixed at node-initialization time and cannot be changed afterward ('that service is using the disk storage path that was specified when the node was initialized') - a real dependency of modify-services on server:node-initialization (minted in initialize-node.json, this batch) that is not modeled as a relation here because no single sentence states it as a requirement of THIS operation rather than as a general fact about storage paths; flagged rather than forced.

cross_component_finding: This page gives the batch's cleanest positive confirmation that ADD/REMOVE-SERVICE rebalance is mechanically the SAME rebalance as node-level rebalance, not a fourth kind: its own CLI section reuses the identical `couchbase-cli rebalance` verb, just with different flags (`--update-services --index-add/--index-remove <nodes>` instead of `--server-add`/`--server-remove`). Combined with manage-data-service-and-rebalance.json's finding that the Data Service has NO equivalent flag at all, the full picture across this batch's five 'X-and-rebalance' pages is: one rebalance primitive, exposed through one CLI verb and one REST controller, parameterized differently depending on whether the trigger is node-level (add/remove/join) or service-level (modify-services) - and the Data Service is the sole exception with no service-level parameterization, forced back to the node-level path.
